paragraphs.en: If you’re like me, when you pick up a compass you can’t help but spin it this way and that, to see if you can trick it. It’s hard to resist experimenting with a spooky force we can’t see or feel ourselves. Yet it always turns the compass needle back towards north.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你像我一样，当你拿起一个指南针时，你会情不自禁地把它转来转去，看看你是否能欺骗它。很难抗拒用一种我们看不到或感觉不到的幽灵力量进行实验。然而，它总是把指南针的指针转回到北方。

paragraphs.en: Even in today’s high-tech world, compasses are useful navigation tools. A compass works without power, unlike GPS, and in any weather and lighting conditions, as opposed to navigation using the Sun, stars or landmarks. If you know which way north is, you can determine any direction.
paragraphs.zh: 即使在当今的高科技世界中，指南针也是有用的导航工具。指南针不像GPS那样需要电源，并且可以在任何天气和照明条件下工作，而不是使用太阳，星星或地标导航。如果你知道北方是哪条路，你可以确定任何方向。

paragraphs.en: Like all cool phenomena, the explanation of how a compass works is not magic – it’s physics. And people have been making use of this particular aspect of physics for more than 2,000 years.
paragraphs.zh: 就像所有很酷的现象一样，对指南针工作原理的解释并不是魔术，而是物理学。人们利用物理学的这一特殊方面已经有2,000多年的历史了。

paragraphs.en: A lodestone spoon
paragraphs.zh: 一个磁石勺子

paragraphs.en: The earliest versions of the compass were developed in ancient China. They were spoon-shaped and made of lodestones, pieces of the naturally magnetic mineral magnetite.
paragraphs.zh: 最早的指南针是在中国古代发明的。它们是用天然磁石制成的勺形指南针。天然磁石是一种天然磁性矿物。

paragraphs.en: When allowed to rotate freely, the spoon handle would align itself with a particular direction (north–south). This was used to organise and harmonise environments, as part of a practice you might know as feng shui.
paragraphs.zh: 当允许它自由旋转时，勺柄会与一个特定的方向（南北）对齐。这是用来组织和协调环境的，作为你可能知道的风水实践的一部分。

paragraphs.en: At the time, it was known that some materials were naturally magnetic – able to attract one another. However, it wasn’t clear exactly what was causing a compass to align itself north–south until 1600, when English physicist William Gilbert deduced that Earth itself acted as a giant magnet.
paragraphs.zh: 当时，人们已经知道某些材料具有天然的磁性--能够相互吸引。然而，直到1600年，英国物理学家威廉·吉尔伯特推断地球本身就像一个巨大的磁铁，人们才确切地知道是什么导致指南针自北向南排列。

paragraphs.en: An invisible field
paragraphs.zh: 一个看不见的领域

paragraphs.en: Like all magnets, Earth generates a magnetic field – an invisible region within which its magnetic forces act.
paragraphs.zh: 像所有的磁铁一样，地球产生磁场-一个看不见的区域，它的磁力作用。

paragraphs.en: Electricity and magnetism are closely connected. Together, they form one of the fundamental interactions in physics: electromagnetism. Magnetic fields can be created by electric currents, which are the movements of charged particles; a changing magnetic field can also induce an electrical current.
paragraphs.zh: 电和磁是紧密相连的。它们共同构成了物理学中最基本的相互作用之一：电磁学。电流可以产生磁场，电流是带电粒子的运动;变化的磁场也可以感应出电流。

paragraphs.en: Our planet spins around an axis once roughly every 24 hours, which is why we have a night and day cycle. The end points of this axis are the North Pole and the South Pole.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的星球大约每24小时绕一个轴旋转一次，这就是为什么我们有一个昼夜循环。这个轴的终点是北极和南极。

paragraphs.en: Beneath Earth’s surface, in the outer core, electrically conducting liquid metals circulate in convective currents. This movement generates electrical currents. Paired with Earth’s rotation around its axis, these currents maintain a global-scale magnetic field. It extends out into space like a giant, invisible bubble, known as the magnetosphere.
paragraphs.zh: 在地球表面之下的外核，导电的液态金属在对流中循环。这种运动产生电流。与地球绕轴旋转相结合，这些电流维持着一个全球规模的磁场。它像一个巨大的不可见的气泡一样延伸到太空中，被称为磁层。

paragraphs.en: And it’s this global-scale magnetic field that allows a compass to work.
paragraphs.zh: 正是这种全球范围的磁场使指南针得以工作。

paragraphs.en: In modern compasses, a magnetised metal needle has replaced the lodestone spoon. That needle is mounted on a low-friction pivot so it has minimal resistance to the effects of external magnetic fields.
paragraphs.zh: 在现代指南针中，磁化的金属针已经取代了天然磁石勺。这种针安装在低摩擦枢轴上，因此它对外部磁场的影响具有最小的阻力。

paragraphs.en: As a result, unless there’s a magnet directly nearby, the needle will align itself with Earth’s magnetic north–south direction.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，除非附近有磁铁，否则磁针将与地球的南北磁场方向对齐。

paragraphs.en: If you’ve ever found that a compass needle didn’t perfectly align with north–south, it might be because it detected a localised magnetic field. Electrical devices such as your phone produce weak magnetic fields. These can affect a compass, causing it to deviate from Earth’s magnetic field.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你曾经发现指南针的指针没有完全对准南北方向，那可能是因为它检测到了一个局部磁场。像你的手机这样的电子设备会产生微弱的磁场。这些磁场会影响指南针，导致它偏离地球的磁场。

paragraphs.en: Which way does a compass really point?
paragraphs.zh: 指南针到底指的是哪条路？

paragraphs.en: All magnets have two opposite points – a “north” pole and a “south” pole. If you have two magnets, opposite poles (north–south) will pull towards each other, while the same poles (south–south or north–north) will push away.
paragraphs.zh: 所有的磁铁都有两个相反的点--一个“北”极和一个“南”极。如果你有两个磁铁，相反的两极（南北）会互相吸引，而相同的两极（南北或南北）会互相推开。

paragraphs.en: The next bit will seem a little confusing, but it’s key to understand why compasses point towards the geographic north.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来的一点似乎有点令人困惑，但这是理解为什么罗盘指向地理北方的关键。

paragraphs.en: Because opposites attract, the “north” arrow on a compass points towards the “south” pole of Earth’s global-scale magnetic field – the area where field lines point down into Earth’s surface. Despite it having a magnetic polarity of “south”, we call this spot the north magnetic pole because it’s located close to the geographic North Pole in the Arctic.
paragraphs.zh: 由于异性相吸，指南针上的“北”箭头指向地球全球磁场的“南”极--也就是磁力线指向地球表面的区域。尽管它的磁极性是“南”，但我们称这个点为北磁极，因为它位于北极的地理北极附近。

paragraphs.en: Earth also has a magnetic south pole, and you guessed it – it’s located near the South Pole in Antarctica, while being the “north” counterpart of Earth’s magnetic field.
paragraphs.zh: 地球也有一个磁南极，你猜对了-它位于南极洲的南极附近，同时是地球磁场的“北”对应物。

paragraphs.en: Useful in more ways than one
paragraphs.zh: 在很多方面都很有用

paragraphs.en: The magnetic poles don’t align perfectly with the poles of Earth’s rotational axis. The reason for this is that Earth’s magnetic field is dynamic. The ever-changing motion of liquid metal in Earth’s outer core means the global magnetic field changes, too.
paragraphs.zh: 磁极与地球自转轴的磁极并不完全一致。这是因为地球的磁场是动态的。地球外核液态金属不断变化的运动意味着全球磁场也会发生变化。

paragraphs.en: In fact, the magnetic north and south poles slowly change their locations, and the entire magnetic field has even flipped its polarity in the past, making the two switch places.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，磁北极和南极慢慢地改变它们的位置，整个磁场甚至在过去翻转了它的极性，使两者交换位置。

paragraphs.en: Earth’s magnetic field also acts as a protective barrier from space weather generated by our Sun: there’s a constant stream of charged particles coming our way, known as solar wind. The global magnetic field helps to shield Earth and our atmosphere.
paragraphs.zh: 地球的磁场也是一个保护屏障，可以抵御太阳产生的太空天气：不断有带电粒子流向我们的方向移动，称为太阳风。全球磁场有助于保护地球和大气层。

paragraphs.en: Mars, by contrast, no longer has a strong global-scale magnetic field to act as a protective shield. Interactions with solar wind have, over time, contributed to the loss of much of Mars’ atmosphere.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下，火星不再有强大的全球磁场作为保护屏障，随着时间的推移，与太阳风的相互作用导致火星大气层的大量流失。

paragraphs.en: So, the same invisible magnetic field that turns a compass needle also plays a much bigger role in helping to keep Earth our home.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，同样的看不见的磁场，使指南针的针也发挥了更大的作用，帮助保持地球我们的家。
